title: W108 Phase A: EXP, LN, LOG10 and LOG against a fresh 396-row live Excel sweep
upstream_status_verbatim: W108 resolved (bit-exact via the x87 backend, removed from tracking)
status_plain: The four log/exp surfaces each carry their own live-Excel row count from one 396-row sweep run after the algorithm had already been determined by a separate 294-row reverse-engineering pass. The source calls the sweep "fresh"; it never uses the words "held out" and never splits a held-out row count, so the held-out state is published as partial with no row split. Two further figures in the same lane are NOT surface pass rates: the 249-row in-crate corpus scores the x87 backend module over EXP and LN only, and the 294/294 scores an out-of-repo reference implementation. The four per-surface figures sum to 381, not the 396 the sentence names.

counts.source_sentence: The `F2XM1`/`FYL2X` last bit is CPU microcode -> on the hardest ~1-in-30 rows, parity is a host-CPU property (validated: AMD Zen2; reference impl 294/294 live Excel).

evidence_locality_note: The 396-row sweep artifact (`x87lab`) and the 294-row corpus (`C:/Temp/ExcelExpFunction`) are outside version control; only `x87_excel_ground_truth.tsv` (the 249 rows) is tracked.
substrate: legacy Microsoft x87 CRT transcendental sequence (`87tran.asm` fFEXP/fFLN/fFLOGm, control word 0x133F, one final store to binary64)
ruled_out: every modern libm for these surfaces: UCRT, glibc, MKL-VML, SVML, and the correctly-rounded value are all ruled out at the bit level (W108:238-240)
the base-2/base-10 special-casing for LOG: `LOG(x, base)` is `ln(x)/ln(base)` for EVERY base, confirmed by the 218-row sweep (W108:249-251)

retractions.withdrawn_on: not withdrawn upstream; contradicted by OxFunc's own git history
retractions.superseded_by: The earliest committed catalogue (commit fc24e93) carries a G1 structural row for EXP (overflow -> +Inf vs Excel #NUM!) and a G2 coercion/array-lift row for LOG. Neither ever held a numeric-exactness row, which is the narrower true claim.

retractions.withdrawn_claim: "`LOG(x, 10)` / `LOG(x, 2)` -- Excel uses dedicated `log10`/`log2` ... OxFunc matches by using `log10`/`log2` directly."
retractions.withdrawn_on: not withdrawn upstream; the two OxFunc documents contradict each other
retractions.superseded_by: The 218-row W108 live sweep refuted it and the special-casing was dropped: `LOG(x, base) = ln(x)/ln(base)` for EVERY base.

open_question: The source calls the sweep 396 rows but its per-surface split totals 381. Where the other 15 rows went is not recoverable from any OxFunc document.
reader_warning: These four counts are per-surface. The 249/249 and 294/294 in the same lane are group totals over EXP and LN, and neither is a worksheet-surface pass rate; neither may be attributed to LOG10, LOG or POWER. Every one of these four surfaces inherits the host-CPU microcode caveat on F2XM1/FYL2X.
